    {
      "quote": "The results demonstrate that tolerable and pharmacologically active dose ranges in clinical studies can be reasonably well predicted from preclinical data.",
      "topic": "Overall prediction accuracy"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Tolerability was best predicted by C max and pharmacologically active ranges by HED or AUC.",
      "topic": "Best predictors"
    },
    {
      "quote": "We noted that despite recommendations by the EMA to base the starting dose on both NOAEL and MABEL, the starting dose is often solely based on the NOAEL.",
      "topic": "Starting dose rationale"
    },
    {
      "quote": "In line with current literature [17], the internal validity of preclinical experiments was poor and preclinical in vivo CNS experiments are often performed without reporting PK results.",
      "topic": "Preclinical reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Thus, a considerable proportion of CNS active agents (28%) seem to have more prominent effects in humans than animals.",
      "topic": "Human vs. animal effects"
    },
    {
      "quote": "These results emphasize that in FIH studies with CNS active compounds, researchers should pay special attention to the psychiatric effects of new compounds, as these cannot be reliably predicted from animal experiments.",
